summary: Both sides are centered, resolution-independent, hue-wheel-cycling radial figures with a white-hot core, but the original is a whipping star of thin curved streamers over a mostly-black field while the port draws concentric expanding RINGS plus a slow spiral arm, filling ~2x more of the rig at ~2.7x the mean brightness and evolving ~7x more slowly.
observations: Control surface matches exactly: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for BOTH sides, and meta.json lists controls: [] on both. Nothing to dial, so the verdict rests entirely on the untouched render (which is the only render obtainable).

Both sides are alive and healthy across every window tried (6 s / 20 fps, 60 s / 5 fps, 240 s / 2 fps, --skip 180): no compile or runtime errors, zeroMotionFrames = 1 (just the first captured frame) on both, brightnessTrend steady/rising, no decay to black, no freeze. Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false both).

No regime rotation on either side. The 240 s / 2 fps survey sheets show the original as the same rayed star and the port as the same ring figure at every one of the 12 sampled times (0-235 s), and a parked late window (rj-late, --skip 180, 20 fps) reproduces the baseline numbers exactly (orig mean 20 motion 5; port mean 51 motion 2). Both patterns' only slow variable is hue.

STRUCTURE, original (rj-grid48 48x48 sheet + rj-radialtrack radial profiles): a blazing white core (r1 = 255, r2 220-249, r3 130-200 of 255) with MONOTONE radial falloff, and 4-8 thin, smoothly curved streamers that reach the edge over an otherwise black field. Outer field (r>=10 on 48x48) averages value 30 with 65% of its pixels at or below 8/255.

STRUCTURE, port: same white core (r1 = 255, r2 213-247) but then a DEEP DARK ANNULUS around r7-r9 (values fall to 0-16) followed by a broad BRIGHT RING further out, plus a persistent bright ring near the rig edge and a white comma/spiral arm near the core. Outer field (r>=10) averages 77 with only 41% near-black. The mid-and-outer field the original leaves black is where the port puts most of its light.

The port's bright ring EXPANDS OUTWARD, which the original never does. Tracking the outer radial-profile peak on 48x48 (rj-radialtrack, 0.5 s dumps): peak at r5 (t=4.0 s) -> r7 (6.0) -> r8 (7.0) -> r9 (7.5-8.0) -> r10 (8.5-9.0) -> r11 (9.5-10.5) -> r12 (11.0-13.0) -> r13 (13.5-14.5), i.e. ~0.8 px/s outward, with an older ring already at r18-r22 during t=0-7 s; ring launch interval looks like ~20 s. The port's rhythm image over 240 s is a stack of regular chevrons (the expanding rings); the original's is flat horizontal stripes with no propagation at all.

RAYS vs RINGS, quantified: azimuthal coefficient of variation on circles of radius 6/9/12/15/18 (48x48, six dump times) is 0.65-3.64 for the original (median ~2.0 - a few bright filaments over darkness) but 0.34-2.22 for the port, dropping to 0.34-0.84 exactly where its ring sits (near-complete rings, azimuthally smooth). The port has no thin radial rays anywhere.

FILL / BRIGHTNESS, default 16x16 rig (rj-dump16, t=1..11 s): pixels above 20/255 are 13-46% of the rig on the original (13/19/26/27/36/46 across the six dumps) vs 49-72% on the port. Mean brightness: orig 18.6 (6 s), 20.0 (60 s), 20.2 (240 s); port 51.2 / 51.3 / 51.7 - the port runs 2.6x brighter, and it is FILL not gain (both cores peg at 255).

MOTION magnitude: at 20 fps orig motion 5.1, motionLit 9.7; port motion 2.0, motionLit 2.4 - a 2.5x deficit on whole-rig churn and 4x on the lit set. Neither is a sparseness artefact (motion and motionLit agree in direction on both sides).

MOTION character, whole-frame spatial autocorrelation vs lag (rj-decorr, 48x48, 0.1 s dumps over 8 s): the original falls to 0.81 at 0.1 s, 0.53 at 0.2 s, 0.35 at 0.3 s and ~0.2 by 0.5 s; the port is still at 0.997 / 0.989 / 0.976 / 0.934 at those lags and does not reach 0.34 until 2.0 s. The port's structure evolves roughly 6-7x more slowly. Visually (48x48 filmstrips, consecutive 20 fps frames): the original's petals visibly grow, curl and dissolve every 0.05 s frame; the port's ring figure is near-identical across the whole 0.55 s strip, with only the inner spiral creeping.

GLOBAL BRIGHTNESS DYNAMICS: the original's mean brightness flickers hard and fast - range 4-51 over 240 s, cv 0.37, autocorrelation of the meanBrightness series already below 0.2 at lag 1.0 s. The port's is smooth and slow - range 18-92, cv 0.27, autocorrelation 0.96 / 0.87 / 0.75 / 0.64 at 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 s and not below 0.2 until 5.0 s. The original's episodic 'eruptions' (moments where the outer field lights to 40-120 and then falls back to 0) have no counterpart in the port's steady output.

COLOUR matches closely. Both walk the entire hue wheel continuously in the same direction (magenta -> red -> orange -> yellow -> green -> cyan -> blue), whole-figure single-hue per frame with a white-desaturated core on both. Unwrapped hue over 240 s: original 18.27 turns -> 13.11 s period; port 19.99 turns -> 11.98 s period (port ~9% faster). Both are fps-invariant on this (orig 13.10 s at 5 fps and 13.11 s at 2 fps; port 11.98 s at both).

No frame-rate coupling on either side: mean brightness over the same 12 s window is identical at 10/20/40 fps (orig 19.4/19.4/19.4; port 65.1/65.1/65.0) and motion halves as fps doubles (orig 9.4/5.1/2.7; port 3.7/2.0/1.0), i.e. per-second change rate ~100 (orig) and ~40 (port) at all three rates. Both are time-based; that axis matches.

Both sides are resolution-independent: at --grid 16x16 and --grid 48x48 each draws the same logical picture, just finer (orig: curved filaments off a white star; port: concentric rings around a spiral hub). Feature counts and sizes scale with the grid on both. That axis matches.

Both sides are seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give identical summary stats on both sides (orig mean 19 motion 5; port mean 51 motion 2), so neither pattern is stochastic and none of the above is an RNG artefact.

Re-judge delta vs the prior verdict (after the 2026-08-29 turbulence-noise de-orphaning, PR #126): the port measurably improved but did not change category. Mean brightness 83 -> 51 (excess 3.8x -> 2.6x), motion 1.4 -> 2.0, and the port now has real texture and a genuine dark annulus instead of a filled disc; the structural decorrelation gap narrowed from ~16x to ~7x. The prior verdict's 'dark core' finding no longer holds - the port's core is now white-hot at 255 like the original's. The rings-instead-of-rays topology, the excess fill, and the placid motion all still hold at the new magnitudes.
feedback: Draw RAYS, not RINGS. This is the single biggest gap. The original is 4-8 thin curved streamers leaving the white core in different directions and reaching the edge; the port is concentric annuli. Measured: azimuthal coefficient of variation on a circle of radius 12 (48x48 grid) is 1.3-3.0 on the original vs 0.34-2.2 on the port, hitting 0.34-0.84 wherever the port's ring sits. Whatever term currently varies with radius alone needs to vary with ANGLE.

Remove the outward-travelling ring. The port launches a bright ring roughly every ~20 s that migrates outward at ~0.8 px/s on a 48x48 grid (peak radius r5 at t=4 s through r13 at t=14.5 s), producing regular chevrons in the rhythm image. The original has no radial propagation whatsoever - its rhythm image is flat horizontal stripes. Any radius-minus-time (r - v*t) travelling-wave term should go.

Kill the dark annulus and restore monotone falloff. The original's radial profile decays monotonically from the core: r1 255 -> r2 ~230 -> r3 ~150 -> r4 ~100 -> r5 ~70 -> r6 ~45 -> low single/low-double digits beyond (48x48 grid). The port dips to 0-16 at r7-r9 and then climbs back to 150-240 at r10-r13. Brightness should just fall away from the core with the streamers riding on top of it.

The field should be mostly black. On the default 16x16 rig the original lights 13-46% of pixels above 20/255 (mean ~28%) and its outer half is near-black 65% of the time; the port lights 49-72% and posts 2.6x the mean brightness (51 vs 20). Target: a few discrete filaments over darkness.

The port is still far too placid. Whole-frame spatial autocorrelation decays to 0.35 in 0.3 s on the original but takes 2.0 s on the port - about 7x too slow. The original's arms visibly re-form every 20 fps frame (motion 5.1, motionLit 9.7 vs port 2.0 / 2.4). Speed up whatever drives streamer shape by roughly 6-7x, or add per-frame turbulence so the arms appear, extend and dissolve on a ~0.3-1 s timescale instead of drifting rigidly.

Add episodic global modulation. The original's total output flickers between near-dark and bright bursts (meanBrightness 4-51 over 240 s, decorrelating in under 1 s) with occasional eruptions where the outer field lights up to 40-120 and then collapses back to 0. The port's output is smooth (18-92, decorrelation 5 s) and never gets dark. Whatever drives the eruptions should also gate total brightness episodically.

Hue is already essentially right - keep it. Both walk the full wheel in the same direction with a white core; just slow the port slightly, from a ~11.98 s cycle to the original's ~13.11 s (measured over 240 s at both 2 and 5 fps on both sides).
Do NOT add controls, and keep the current time-based (fps-invariant) and resolution-independent behaviour: both sides already match on all three of those axes.
